question.text: In a closed organ pipe, the frequency of fundamental note is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. A certain amount of water is now poured in the organ pipe so that the fundamental frequency is increased to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>110</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. If the organ pipe has a cross-sectional area of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, the amount of water poured in the organ tube is ________<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math>. (Take speed of sound in air is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>330</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> )

solution.text:
Fundamental frequency for closed organ pipe in the first part:

V4l1=30⇒l1=114 m

Similarly, for second part:

V4l2=110⇒l2=34 m

Therefore, change in length Δl=2 m

Change in volume =AΔl=400 cm3

M=400 g;∵ρ=1 g cm-3
